title: The 5 Tallest Roller Coasters Ever Built, Ranked (#2 Was Blown Up)

scenes.text: The five tallest roller coasters ever built, ranked. The old champion was demolished with explosives last year.

scenes.label: Fury 325 · 99 m
scenes.text: Number five: Fury 325 in North Carolina. 99 metres, that's 325 feet, and it opened in 2015.

scenes.label: Red Force · 112 m
scenes.text: Number four: Red Force at Ferrari Land in Spain. 112 metres of vertical tower, opened in 2017.

scenes.label: Top Thrill 2 · 128 m
scenes.text: Number three: Top Thrill 2 at Cedar Point in Ohio. 128 metres, and since 2024 it fires riders backwards up the tower too.

scenes.label: Kingda Ka · 139 m
scenes.text: Number two: Kingda Ka in New Jersey. 139 metres, the world's tallest for twenty years, until explosives brought it down in February 2025.

scenes.label: Falcon's Flight · 163 m
scenes.text: Number one: Falcon's Flight in Saudi Arabia. 163 metres tall, 155 miles an hour, opened on New Year's Eve 2025. Nothing else comes close.

description:
The five tallest roller coasters ever built, ranked by height.
Falcon's Flight at Six Flags Qiddiya City near Riyadh opened on 31 December 2025 at 163 metres (535 feet) and 250 km/h (155 mph), the tallest, fastest and longest coaster ever. Kingda Ka at Six Flags Great Adventure held the height record at 139 metres (456 feet) from 2005 until it was demolished on 28 February 2025. Top Thrill 2 at Cedar Point stands 128 metres, Red Force at Ferrari Land 112 metres, and Fury 325 at Carowinds 99 metres.
Which of these would you actually dare to ride?
first_comment: Falcon's Flight is also the longest coaster ever at 4,250 metres of track, more than two and a half miles. Which would you put at number one, and what should we rank next?
